sylvie.title: Crab Patrol
sylvie.ask: The crab runts are back on the beach, nipping at anything that moves. Thin them out? Four should do.
sylvie.thanks: That's the beach quiet for a day or two.

sylvie.title: Tusks in the Woodpile
sylvie.ask: Two grunt runts have been rooting through my woodpile again. Chase them off. Properly.
sylvie.thanks: Good. Let them grumble somewhere else.

sylvie.title: Kindling
sylvie.ask: Fifteen wood, if you're passing a tree. The stove eats it faster than I can split it.
sylvie.thanks: Bless you. Here, for your trouble.

sylvie.title: Stone for the Wall
sylvie.ask: The garden wall's coming down a stone at a time. Twelve stones would patch it.

sylvie.title: Jam Season
sylvie.ask: Ten handfuls of berries and I'll make jam. You'll get some. Probably.

sylvie.title: Something for Supper
sylvie.ask: Eight brown mushrooms. The plain ones. Not the red ones, whatever they tell you.
sylvie.thanks: Supper's sorted. Take this, just in case.

sylvie.title: Eyes in the Trees
sylvie.ask: Two prowlers have been watching my house from the plains' edge. I don't like being watched.
sylvie.thanks: Good. I can sleep with the shutters open again.

sylvie.title: Shells for the Roof
sylvie.ask: Ten shells. Crab or tortoise, I'm not fussy. They make better roof tiles than you'd think.
sylvie.thanks: That roof's going to outlast me.

heidi.title: Bears at the Berries
heidi.ask: Two bears are guarding the berry patch like it's theirs. I can calm one. Not two. Would you?
heidi.thanks: They'll sulk, but they'll live. Thank you.

heidi.title: Grove Patrol
heidi.ask: Something's got everything in the grove on edge. Walk it for me? Four of the angriest ones.
heidi.thanks: Quieter already. I can hear the birds again.

heidi.title: Pine Resin
heidi.ask: Three lumps of pine resin. It seals a wound better than anything I can buy.

heidi.title: Herbs for the Remedy
heidi.ask: Six bunches of wild herbs. They grow among the berry bushes, if you look.
heidi.thanks: These are lovely. I'll make two batches.

heidi.title: Bark for Bandages
heidi.ask: Birch bark, three strips. Soft on the inside, and it keeps a dressing clean.
heidi.thanks: Thank you. Someone will be glad of these.

heidi.title: Little Dragon, Big Temper
heidi.ask: There's a dragonling on the rocks past the grove, and it's scorching anything that wanders close. Please be careful.
heidi.thanks: You came back. Good. That's all I wanted.

marisol.title: Something for the Pot
marisol.ask: Six crab meat. If the bay won't feed us, the crabs will.
marisol.thanks: That's supper for three houses. Thank you.

marisol.title: Off My Beach
marisol.ask: Two crabscallions are sitting on my best mooring like they own it. Move them.
marisol.thanks: Ha! Let them sulk in the deep.

marisol.title: Sea Glass
marisol.ask: Three bits of sea glass. My daughter strings them. Don't tell her I asked.
marisol.thanks: She'll think the sea brought them. Let her.

brann.title: Ore for the Forge
brann.ask: Ten iron ore. I pay for it either way, but this way you get a favour too.
brann.thanks: Good ore. Clean. I'll remember who brought it.

brann.title: Leather for Grips
brann.ask: Six boar hides. Every hilt in Saltmere needs a new grip and the boar-men keep theirs.

brann.title: Charcoal Wood
brann.ask: Thirty wood for the charcoal pit. Boring, I know. Fire doesn't care.
brann.thanks: The pit thanks you. So do I.

tova.title: Tar for the Nets
tova.ask: Four lumps of pine resin. I boil it into tar for the nets. The old way.

tova.title: Birch for the Floats
tova.ask: Five strips of birch bark. Floats, child. Nets need floats.

tova.title: My Knees
tova.ask: Eight bunches of wild herbs. For a poultice. My knees are older than the drill and twice as loud.
tova.thanks: Bless you. Now go, before I start telling stories.

aurelie.title: Frightened Children
aurelie.ask: The boar-men wander too close to the houses. Two of them, please. The children won't play outside.
aurelie.thanks: Thank you. I'll tell the children it's safe.

aurelie.title: Bread for the Shrine
aurelie.ask: Five loaves of seed bread for the shrine's table. Anyone hungry may take one.
aurelie.thanks: Someone will eat well tonight because of you.
